question: Which of these does a green plant need in order to make food?
options: Light
Soil
Wind
Sound

question: A metal ball passes easily through a metal ring at room temperature. The ball is heated strongly for two minutes and then no longer passes through the ring. Why not?
options: The ball expanded when it was heated.
The ball became heavier when it was heated.
The ring contracted when the ball was heated.
The ball melted slightly at its surface.

question: A torch shines on a ball and a shadow is formed on a screen behind it. The ball is then moved closer to the torch, without moving the torch or the screen. What happens to the shadow on the screen?
options: It becomes larger.
It becomes smaller.
It stays exactly the same size.
It disappears completely.

question: A battery-powered torch is switched on. Which energy conversion takes place in the torch bulb?
options: Electrical energy to light energy and heat energy
Electrical energy to light energy only
Chemical energy to light energy only
Light energy to electrical energy

question: Two blocks are placed in water. Block A floats. Block B sinks. Both blocks have exactly the same mass. Which statement must be true?
options: Block A takes up more space than block B.
Block A is heavier than block B.
Block B takes up more space than block A.
Block B is made of metal.

question: A cactus lives in a hot, dry desert. Its leaves are reduced to thin spines. How does this help the cactus to survive?
options: It loses less water to the surroundings.
It can absorb more water from the air.
It can make more food in the day.
It keeps the cactus cool at night.

question: In a circuit with one battery, one switch and two bulbs arranged in a single loop, one bulb is removed from its holder. What happens to the other bulb?
options: It goes out, because the circuit is now open.
It becomes brighter, because it gets all the electricity.
It stays exactly as bright as before.
It becomes dimmer but stays lit.

question: A glass of iced water is left on a table in a room. After ten minutes, droplets of water are seen on the outside of the glass. Explain how the droplets of water were formed.
A gardener removes all the insects from a greenhouse containing flowering plants. After some months, he notices that the plants produce far fewer fruits than before. Explain why.

Two identical cups are filled with the same amount of hot water at the same temperature. Cup A is wrapped in a thick towel and cup B is left uncovered. After 20 minutes, explain which cup contains water at a higher temperature and why.
